correctness.rationale: Over a splitting field, character orthogonality gives E_a E_b=E_{-a} exactly when b=-2a. For b different from -2a the two Leibniz terms have distinct output indices b/2 and -a. Their coefficients vanish separately, killing every off-diagonal entry. The remaining scalar identities are equivalent to t_0=0, t_{-a}=-t_a and t_{2a}=2t_a. Doubling is invertible on indices even in characteristic two, so that characteristic vanishes, as does characteristic zero by finite doubling periodicity. On indices of additive order m, the group generated by 2 and -1 acts freely. Iteration around each doubling orbit and possible identification with its negative give exactly the two ordinary-integer divisibility conditions. Nullity is invariant under the field extension and diagonality implies commutativity. For n=3,5,7,9 the consistency integers introduce no prime coprime to n; for n=11 the integer is 33 and there is one orbit. For the character operator set u=k-2j+i in the coefficient identity: the three arguments are u,-u,u/2 and chi(-1)=chi(2)=-1, hence the difference is 3chi(u). An independent direct Leibniz-matrix replay at n=11 in F_3 found rank 120 for 121 variables and passed all 1331 witness coefficient tests.
residual_risks: The independent replay checks only the n=11, characteristic-three certificate. The dimension for unbounded orders rests on the proof. No claim is made for characteristic dividing n or even n.
